title: Ops-ready inference sales cribsheet - field kit
body:
Purpose:
Quick, operational cribsheet for technical sellers and SDRs to run short customer conversations, triage fit, and propose an initial Redwood configuration. Not a full playbook — use during calls / handoff to SEs.

Use cases this doc is for:
- Fast qualification (5–10 min) for Platform / Product / Infra buyers
- Rapid proposal of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options with immediate next steps
- Field reference for latency/cost tradeoffs and fallback options when customers have hard constraints

30-second pitch (single-sentence):
Redwood Inference gives your engineering team predictable, high-throughput LLM inference across hosted, reserved, and private deployments — so you get production latency, lower token spend through smart caching/batching, and the safety/compliance posture you need without building a custom serving stack.

Top-line TL;DR (technical):
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized, continuous batching, KV cache and prefix caching out-of-the-box
- Routing: policy-driven (latency/cost/region/customer tier) with automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants
- Deployment modes: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput + committed pricing), Private (VPC/on-prem with KMS integrations)

Typical qual flow + quick hints:
1) What are latency SLOs? (p95 target, interactive vs async)
   - If <300ms p95: need Dedicated or Private + small-sequence configs; ask about concurrency patterns.
2) Expected throughput / qps? (tokens per minute/day)
   - High sustained qps + tight SLOs => Dedicated recommended.
3) Data sensitivity / compliance? (PHI/PCI/enterprise IP)
   - If regulated => Private (VPC or on-prem) or Dedicated with stricter ingress/egress controls.
4) Budget posture: bursty vs predictable spend?
   - Bursty, exploratory => Hosted with burst capacity. Predictable, scale => Reserved commitments on Dedicated.

Fast objection responses (concise):
- "Why not just run open-source model ourselves?"
  - Short: You can, but production inference cost and reliability are where teams get stuck; we provide optimized kernels, autoscaling, fallback model variants, and observability so you don't build and operate an inference stack.
- "What about vendor lock-in?"
  - We expose standard APIs, allow model pinning, and support private deployments; you control model versions and can export latency/cost artifacts.
- "How secure is Private?"
  - Private options include customer-managed VPC, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs. We run control plane connectors you can review in audits.

Quick fallback matrix (one-look):
- Latency-critical + predictable throughput => Dedicated with small-batch, KV caching enabled
- Low-cost, tolerant latency => Hosted with aggressive batching + 4-bit quantized model variant
- Regulated data => Private (VPC) + no-hosted-data retention + enterprise SLA
- Capacity spikes => Autoscaling + burst pool or temporary routed to hosted fallback

Negotiation-ready cost ballparks (field estimates; call finance for quotes):
- Hosted API (small app): $0.02–$0.12 / 1k tokens depending on model family and streaming
- Dedicated (reserved small cluster): ~$20k–$80k / month (depends on GPU mix + throughput SLO)
- Private (on-prem + license): one-time platform fee + support; range varies heavily by deployment size — escalate to AE for a scoped estimate

Config cheat sheet (what to propose on first call):
- MVP conversational assistant (low concurrency): Hosted, mid-size model, enable prefix caching, 1s timeout
- High-throughput QA / embeddings pipeline: Dedicated with batching profile tuned for 256–512 seqs, KV cache + async workers for embeddings
- PHI-sensitive triage: Private deployment, strict egress rules, per-route audit logging, invite Security SE for deep dive

Canary + rollout quick checklist (one-pager for SE handoff):
- Define target traffic % for canary (5–10%)
- Establish quality metrics and baseline prompt set (seed 50 prompts)
- Set latency & error alert thresholds in Console (p95 SLA + token-cost baseline)
- Configure automated fallback to lower-cost variant on errors/timeouts
- Schedule 48h monitoring window and post-rollout regression eval

Common technical signals to escalate to SRE/Platform: 
- Sustained token cost > estimate by 30%
- p95 latency > SLO consistently for 15+ minutes
- Model OOMs or GPU allocation errors in Dedicated clusters

Sample call snippets (copy-paste friendly):
- "What's your typical request size and peak concurrency? That helps me recommend a batch profile and whether Dedicated makes sense."
- "Do you have any data residency or compliance mandates? If yes, we should review Private options early."

Prompt & eval quick-start (for demo/proof-of-concept):
- Starter eval set (50 prompts): 20 product Q&A, 20 knowledge-search, 10 multi-turn follow-ups
- Metrics to capture: latency p50/p95, token cost per request, hallucination rate (binary check), failure rate

Speaker notes / slide flow for a 10-min technical sales demo:
1) 60s: 2-slide problem framing (cost/latency/ops overhead)
2) 90s: Redwood technical differentiators (runtime, routing, caching)
3) 2m: Live demo showing hosted API vs dedicated perf numbers (need perf artifacts)
4) 2m: Config recommendation for customer type (example mapping)
5) 1m: Risk mitigation + fallback policies
6) 60s: Next steps & scoping ask (tokens/day, SLOs, compliance)

Open TODOs (for SE / PM follow-up):
- Add up-to-date pricing ranges from Finance (ACTION: Julian)
- Attach model perf benchmark table for small/mid/large families (ACTION: Eng perf team)
- Create a 1-page printable cheat sheet for field (ACTION: Design)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep examples short and concrete; customers want numbers (p95, qps, rough $/month)
- Avoid internal jargon in early calls — use "Reserved" instead of "Committed capacity" when talking to procurement

Quick links (for handoff):
- Internal perf artifacts: confluence/INFERENCE/perf-2026 (ask Eng for latest link)
- Playbook: confluence/INFERENCE/sales-root (full flows & pitch decks)

Revision history:
- 2025-11-05 initial sketch by Maya Chen
- 2026-01-12 added fallback matrix (Julian)
- 2026-02-22 price placeholders updated; set status -> in_review

End of cribsheet. Keep this lightweight — main aim: get to a scoped next step and hand off to SE with concrete numbers.
